statements.status_notes: Fixed in 0.1.2: grubx64.efi is built from source (build/grub/: Ubuntu grub2 2.14-2ubuntu3 + build/grub/patches) and embeds grub,6, which meets shim's SbatLevel 2025112400. build/grub/grubsrc.py proves on every build that each fix grub,6 stands for (CVE-2025-54770, -54771, -61661, -61662, -61663, -61664) is present by reverse-applying its upstream commit, and refuses the claim otherwise (manifest secure_boot.sbat_version_check; build/grub/security-fixes.json).

Fixed in 0.1.2: BOOTX64.EFI is Debian's shim 16.1 (shim-signed 1.51+16.1-2, SHA-256-pinned in build/shim/debian-shim.lock), carrying two Microsoft signatures over the same Authenticode digest, one chaining to Microsoft Corporation UEFI CA 2011 and one to Microsoft UEFI CA 2023 (build/shim/microsoft-uefi-ca-{2011,2023}.pem). build/build.sh and build/verify-dist.sh refuse a shim without both; the scan's shim CA check sees both chains.

statements.impact_statement: The flaw lets a device with a copied UUID bypass GRUB's password check. beast-boot's GRUB configuration sets no superusers and no password (grub/ has no 'set superusers' or password_pbkdf2), so there is no password check to bypass.
poplib is never imported: the bundled Python runs only the beast-boot app (installer/beastbooter, packaging/portable), which has no poplib import.
expat 2.8.5 is in the Windows runtime only. The app parses XML only in installer/beastbooter/platforms/darwin.py (plistlib, macOS), so on Windows pyexpat's XML_ParseBuffer is never called.

statements.impact_statement: The flaw is in gz_vacate/gzprintf in zlib's gzwrite.c (zlib 1.3.1.2 to 1.3.2). Checked in the four python-build-standalone 20261021 runtimes pinned in packaging/portable/runtimes.lock: Linux and macOS link zlib 1.3.2 statically, but gzwrite.c is not linked in: no file in those archives contains its error strings ('requested length does not fit in int', 'request does not fit in a size_t', 'internal error: deflate stream corrupt') or any gzwrite/gzprintf/gzvprintf name. Windows ships DLLs/zlib1.dll version 1.3.1, below the affected range, and its only importer, tcl86t.dll, imports just deflate/inflate/crc32/adler32/zlibVersion/zError (objdump -p). CPython's zlib module uses only the deflate/inflate API.

The flaw is in gz_vacate (gzwrite with non-blocking writes). None of the 62 ELF files in the beast-net initramfs imports gzwrite, gzopen, gzdopen, gzprintf, gzputs, gzputc, gzflush or gzclose_w (checked with readelf --dyn-syms on dist/esp/beast-net/initrd.img, 0.1.0); CPython's zlib module uses only the deflate/inflate API.

Build/test tooling only, never on the drive. The flaw is in QEMU's virtio-gpu device (2D image allocation). beast-boot starts QEMU only from devtools/bbdev/qemu.py (e2e tests, make vm, screenshots), devtools/gdb/demo.py and beastnet/tests/qemu_smoke.py; all use '-nodefaults -device VGA' or the x86 machine default (standard VGA) and never create a virtio-gpu, virtio-vga or virtio-gpu-gl device (grep of every '-device'/'-vga' argument in the repository).

Test firmware only (OVMF for the QEMU test VMs), never on the drive. The flaw is in OpenSSL's DTLS retransmission. EDK2 builds its OpenSSL with no-dtls, no-dtls1-method, no-dtls1_2-method and no-dgram (CryptoPkg/Library/OpensslLib/configure.py, edk2-stable202511, which ovmf 2025.11 is built from), so no DTLS method or connection exists in the firmware; the tests also never use HTTPS boot, the only TLS user in OVMF.

Test firmware only (OVMF for beast-boot's own QEMU test VMs), never on the drive. EDK2's Pkcs7Verify does call PKCS7_verify, so the code is present; a crafted SignedData with an empty digestAlgorithms SET is needed to reach it. In the e2e tests the firmware verifies only Debian's shim-signed 1.51+16.1-2 (SHA-256-pinned in build/shim/debian-shim.lock), its MokManager, and PE images the tests build themselves. The one other path is a developer chainloading an untrusted ISO's EFI program in `make vm` with Secure Boot on; the use-after-free then stays inside that QEMU guest. Ubuntu's tracker lists edk2 as needs-triage for every release (2026-10-25); re-check when it is triaged.

statements.impact_statement: beast-net helper kernel 7.3.0-9.9 (upstream base v7.3-rc6; the fix landed in v7.3, Ubuntu: pending 7.3.0-10.10). The use-after-free is in TCP request-socket handling (tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock, tcp_check_req, ip_options_build with saved IP options), so it needs a listening TCP socket that receives SYNs with IP options, or request-socket migration (net.ipv4.tcp_migrate_req=1, default 0, or a BPF_SK_REUSEPORT_SELECT_OR_MIGRATE program). The helper never listens on TCP: its processes are init, the beastnet app (outgoing HTTPS only; its only bind() is the AF_UNIX wpa_supplicant control socket, beastnet/python/beastnet/wifi.py), udhcpc and wpa_supplicant; no server program runs (busybox httpd and netstat are removed, build/beastnet/userland.list). A network attacker therefore cannot reach the code. It is reachable only if the person at the console deliberately starts a TCP listener from the helper's maintenance shell (root, with physical access). Re-check, and move to the fixed kernel, when 7.3.0-10.10 reaches stonking-updates/-security.

statements.status_notes: Reviewed 2026-10-25: shim 16.1 dp.c is_removable_media_path() passes DevicePathToStr(li->FilePath) to StrnCaseCmp() without a NULL check, and it runs on every boot of the stick (esp/EFI/BOOT/BOOTX64.EFI is on the removable-media path: shim.c should_use_fallback(), mok.c). DevicePathToStr returns NULL only when the firmware's pool allocation fails; the boot then hangs or crashes, or on firmware without NULL-page protection the removable-path/fallback check may misjudge. Every image shim loads is still verified, so it is no Secure Boot bypass. CVSS 3.1 3.9 (AV:L/AC:H/PR:H), Debian severity negligible. Reaches the drive through deb-src:shim@16.1-2, the Built-Using of shim-signed 1.51+16.1-2.
